description: Copy of a letter from W. H. Hughes, Jr., Director of Corporate Income and Franchise Tax Division at the State of North Carolina Department of Revenue. The letter was sent to Mr. Thomas L. Norris, Jr. and The Raleigh Fine Arts Society, Inc. on October 8, 1965. The letter includes details of franchise and income tax exemptions for The Raleigh Fine Arts Society, Inc.

Copy of a list of recommended procedures for restoring the Smithsonian Dentzel Carousel. List was developed July 30-August 1, 1974. Recommendations include procedures for paint stripping and structural repairs.

Invoice from Fisher Scientific Company, Raleigh, NC 27604, to Pullen Park Restoration, Parks & Recreation, W.W. Farley, Raleigh, NC. Invoice for calcium chloride 4-20 mesh 1KG. The front has details of the order and the shipment. The back has a list of 35 branch and plant addresses.
List of nine plaques from the Pullen Park Carousel and seventeen large murals on panels. Four letters were corrected in blue pen (Masted, Scene, Leopard, Leopard).
Blank paper with letterhead that reads: "William W. Farley, M.D., F.A.A.P., 1300 St. Mary's Street, Raleigh, N.C. 27605, Telephone 833-3689."

Blank paper with letterhead that reads: "North Carolina Medical Society, William W. Farley, M.D., Chairman, Section on Pediatrics, 1300 St. Mary's Street, Raleigh, North Carolina 27605. The letterhead also has an image of the NC Medical Society building.

Blank paper with letterhead that reads: "North Carolina Medical Society, William W. Farley, M.D., Chairman, Section on Pediatrics, 1300 St. Mary's Street, Raleigh, North Carolina 27605. The letterhead also has an image of the NC Medical Society building.

Blank paper with letterhead that reads: "Rex Hospital, 1311 Saint Mary's Street, Raleigh, North Carolina 27603." The letterhead also has an image of Rex Hospital. The bottom of the paper has text that reads: "A Voluntary, Non-Profit, Community Hospital Contributing to Community Health Since 1894."

Folded notecard from Silvia Bell and The West Hills Community Club. The front is green with an image of a round tree with flowers and three white doves. The inside has text that reads: "Dear Sir: The West Laurel Hills Community Club will like to donate this check - $25 - for the restoration of the carrousel. Sincerely yours, Silvia Bell." There is also an address written on the inside: 4006 Spruce Drive, Raleigh, N.C. 27612. The back has information about the design in English and French.

Raleigh Fine Arts Society card from April 21, 1976. Handwritten text on the front reads: "Fine Arts Society 111 served of 4.00 per person, Total 444, Mr. Fred Benson, 40 Ral. City Club, Sir Walter Hotel, #196 4/21/76." Text on the back reads: "Susan Sink."

A Guide to Federal Programs for Historic Preservation, 1976 Supplement, Office of Preservation Services, The Preservation Press, The National Trust for Historic Preservation. Packet was sent from the office of Jesse Helms, United States Senator. Four pages total, stapled in the top left corner.

Copy of part of a Significance Form for the National Register of Historic Places. Includes a statement of significance for the Pullen Park Carousel, built by the Pennsylvania Carousel Company of Gustav A. Dentzel and his master carver, Salvatore Cernigliaro around 1900. Carousel was moved to Pullen Park by July 30, 1915. The statement of significance is circled, and the following text is cut off.
Resume for Gordon L. Newby. Includes his education, work experience, and examples of his restoration work. Two pages total, stapled in the top left corner.

Copy of the National Register of Historic Places Inventory - Nomination Form for the Pullen Park Carousel. Includes overall description of the carousel, individual descriptions of each animal, statement of significance, and other information. Fourteen pages total, stapled in the top left corner.

Letter to Mr. Bradshaw from Mrs. Cy Farley, Chairman of the Carousel Restoration, Raleigh Fine Arts Society. The letter is dated to May 17, 1976, it thanks Mr. Bradshaw for being an advisor on the committee and provides more information relevant to the project. The letter is edited in green pen, and at the bottom of the page there is a list of people to send a copy of the letter to.

Letter to Mrs. W.W. Farley from Gordon D. Newby from the Department of Mediterranean Studies at the Brandeis University Graduate School of Arts and Sciences in Waltham, Massachusetts. The letter is dated to July 14, 1976, and discusses Gordon D. Newby's father, Gordon L. Newby as a potential restorer for the Pullen Park Carousel. The letter includes information about Newby's upcoming move to Raleigh and contact information for his father. Signed by Newby at the bottom.

Progress report to the Civic Committee to Restore the Pullen Park Carousel from Cy Farley, Raleigh Fine Arts Society Chairman on August 31, 1976. The report includes a list of eight decisions that were made at the June 29, 1976 meeting. The report has some annotations made in purple ink, including underlining and notes in the margin. Two pages total, stapled in the top left corner.

Copy of a letter from the Division of Archives and History of the State of North Carolina Department of Cultural Resources to Mrs. James B. Turner Jr., President of the Raleigh Fine Arts Society. Annotations were made on the letter in purple ink, including underlining and notes in the margin. Attached is a copy of the first page of an application for a Request for Historic Preservation Grant-In-Aid for the Pullen Park Carousel. The two pages are stapled in the top left corner.

Copy of a letter from Thomas C. Layton to Mrs. Farley, dated to December 6, 1976. The letter confirms the terms of work to restore the Pullen Park Carousel, along with price estimates. Signed by Layton at the end of the letter. Two of the price numbers were circled in black ink. Three pages total, stapled in the top left corner.
Ink pen sketch on thin brown tracing paper of the exterior view of the Pullen Park Carousel.

Copy of a manual for "Suggestions on Handling Epoxies Safely." Includes precautions, descriptions of certain epoxies, and procedure information including mixing and application suggestions, for example. Seven pages total, stapled in the top left corner.

Advertisement booklet for Interlux Yacht Paints. The front cover has a photograph of an underwater scene with a boat at the surface and a person swimming underneath of it. The inside includes lists of Anti-Fouling Bottom Paints, Topside Enamels, and Specialty Finishes. The back has a chart for the Interlux Antifouling Paint Application Guide.
Bank deposit slip for the State Bank of Raleigh for $285.00. "Merry-Go-Round" is written on the slip in black ink.

Brochure for "And Then Came Christmas," an album for an automated music machine recorded by Paul R. Eakins. The front has a list of songs played on sides A and B. The brochure unfolds and the inside has information about seven music machines and the album, "And Then Came Christmas." The back has information about Paul R. Eakins and the Gay 90's Village.

Membership card for Marriott's Great America Carousel Club. Red and blue text on white card. The front has information about membership and benefits, along with a small image of a carousel. The membership card is good through 12/31/77.

List of "Suggested Sources of Supplies and Assistance in Maintaining Your Merry Go Round or Individual Figures." Includes sources and notes about how they each could be helpful. Printed in purple ink. Notes were written in the margins with black ink.
List of "Restoration Suppliers Prepared by The Collector's Committee." Printed on yellow paper. Includes things like glue, horsehair tails, jewels, etc., and locations of where to get them.
"Armitage-Herschell-Spillman Company" a chronology by Barbara Fahs Charles. Timeline from 1873-1945 of the company. Two pages total, stapled in the top left corner.

Handwritten note from Carolyn Cunningham that reads: "This comes from the company that my husband Henry works with and that Bill Granberry is President of - it was not one that I was given to contact but thought it might not hurt to ask. Carolyn Cunningham. P.S. You also received a check for $25.00 from Garden Friends, a garden club that many RPA members belong to." Written on grey paper with printed blue text at the top: "Edwards & Broughton Co., Raleigh, North Carolina."
Copy of a resume for Rosa Patton Ragan from 1965-1977. Includes experience in painting, drawing, photograph, teaching, research, and more.

Note to Mrs. Farley from Elizabeth Harrison, Secretary of the Martin 76'ers on January 5, 1977. The note reads: "Dear Mrs. Farley, The Martin 76'ers would like to invite you to give a talk on the Pullen Park Carousel project at our meeting Jan. 12 at 2:40 in our music room. Would this be convenient with you? Please let Mrs. Kennedy know by contacting her at the school. Thank you and we hope you are able to come. Sincerely, Elizabeth Harrison, Secretary of the Martin 76'ers." Note is written in blue ink on paper with a letterhead that reads: "Martin 76'ers, LeRoy Martin Junior High School, 1701 Ridge Road, Raleigh, North Carolina 27607."

Handwritten letter addressed to "best speaker" (Mrs. Farley), signed "Love, all of us at Martin," dated to January 14, 1977. The letter thanks Mrs. Farley for her visit and provides updates of what to expect at the January 18th council meeting. The letter is written in black ink on paper with a letterhead that reads: "Mrs. Frank Ramsey Kennedy, 2634 Saint Mary's Street, Raleigh, North Carolina 27609." Two pages total. 

a) letter
b) accompanying envelope

Envelope addressed to Mrs. W. W. Farley at 2625 Dover Road, Raleigh, N.C. 27608, stamped with the date January 15, 1977. The return address on the back reads: "Mrs. Frank Ramsey Kennedy, 2634 Saint Mary's Street, Raleigh, North Carolina 27609. The inside of the envelope is blue. 

a) letter
b) envelope
Parks and Recreation Advisory Committee minutes from the January 19, 1977, 4pm meeting. Notes include the Shelley Sertoma Park Master Plan and the Pullen Carousel - Stabilization Restoration.

Typed letter to the Friends of the Merry-Go-Round from Cy Farley with the Raleigh Fine Arts Society, Inc., dated to February 28, 1977. The letter talks about the Pullen Park Carousel and its need for restoration and ends with a call for help/request for funds to the Merry-Go-Round Restoration. The letter is two pages total (a-b). Signed by Cy Farley on the bottom of the second page. The first page has a letterhead that reads: "Merry-Go-Round Restoration, P.O. Box 19515, Raleigh, North Carolina 27609."

Copy of an interoffice memo from the Parks and Recreation Director to the City Manager on March 4, 1977. The memo largely discusses the necessary finances for the carousel restoration and some general details of the project. Five people are cc'd, including Mrs. Cy Farley. Blue pen marks bracket a section of the letter about the process of getting the carousel on the Register of National Historic Sites and the unanimous agreement to find funding for the initiation of the carousel restoration.

Handwritten letter in green ink from Annie Hoover Peden (Mrs. J.M.) to Mrs. Wm. Farley, dated to March 12, 1977. The letter reads: "Dear Mrs. Farley: Mr. Peden and I would like to pledge three thousand dollars ($3,000) toward the restoration of the __ in Pullen Park. Please let us know when you will need payment. Yours very truly, (Mrs. J.M.) Annie Hoover Peden."

Copy of the minutes from the City Council of the City of Raleigh meeting on Tuesday, March 15, 1977, at 6pm. Among other notes, the minutes discuss the funds and the use of those funds for the carousel restoration. Two pages total (a-b).

Copy of page 3 of a memo from John W. Kinney, Jr. with the State of North Carolina Department of Cultural Resources to Margaret Stephenson on March 22, 1977. The memo discusses the options and implications of installing security doors for the Pullen Park Carousel. A section of the text toward the bottom is underlined in blue ink.

Copy of page 1 of 2 of the Cost Estimate/Design Development Phase for Pullen Park/Phase III Site Improvements from April 15, 1977. Sections I.-V. are listed. Section III lists the carousel and related details along with a price estimate of $33,990. Each section number and price has been circled and all of the text related to section III has also been circled.

Check stub/bank statement from American Mortgage Insurance Company - Raleigh, N.C., for Contribution to Restoring Pullen Park Carousel 1977. $250.00, dated to May 9, 1977.

a) bank statement
b) envelope

Envelope addressed to Merry-Go-Round Restoration, Post Office Box 19515, Raleigh, North Carolina 27609 from American Mortgage Insurance Company. The front has been stamped twice in red ink and dated to May 11, 1977. The back has writing in blue ink that says "Pauline - call, Jean Smith - called." A small pink "C5" is on the back as well. 

a) bank statement
b) envelope

Copy of page 1 of 2 of a Cost Estimate/Design Development Phase for Pullen Park Phase III Site Improvements from April 15, 1977. "III. Carousel" has been circled, along with number and prices for I.-V. Purple writing at the top reads "From P. and Rec. Dir. to City Manager 5-13-77." Part a. under section III. has been circled with a note that says "??? we did this free."

Typed letter from Thomas C. Layton to Ms. Margaret L. Stephenson, North Carolina Department of Natural Resources, Raleigh, North Carolina 27611, dated to May 19, 1977. The letter is five pages long, stapled in the left corner, and discusses restoration details from the proposal. It also answers questions that Ms. Stephenson had. Much of the information is about paint selection and procedures.

Copy of a letter from Richard C. Mehring, Acting Department Consultant for Historic Architecture, Technical Preservation Services Division, to Mrs. William Farley on July 26, 1977. The letter indicates that the grant recipient can be transferred from the Raleigh Fine Arts Society to the City of Raleigh.  The letter also talks about the paint research and re-coating of the animals on the Pullen Park Carousel. At the top, "Ann of Ohio," is written in blue ink. "Who made the proposal" is written in the right margin, with a line pointing towards a bracketed and underlined portion of the letter. Signed at the bottom by Richard C. Mehring.

Copy of a letter from Janet K. Seapker, Archaeology & Historic Preservation Section of the North Carolina Department of Cultural Resources, to Mrs. William W. Farley on August 10, 1977. The letter includes four items for Cathy Leach to include in her bid for paint research on the Pullen Park Carousel animals. Signed by Janet K. Seapker at the bottom.

Copy of a letter sent to Bruce from Cy Farley on August 29, 1977, that reads: "Dear Bruce -- The film is marvelous! I am assuming that we may use it on T.V. here in Ral -- God! Do I have further questions! How do you suggest we discuss it - ? letter - ? Phone? After 5 - If I must call you -- Thanks again for the lifeline -- I feel like we are drowning - Sincerely - Cy Farley."

Copy of a letter to Mrs. William W. Farley from Peter B. Sandbeck, Restoration Specialist at the North Carolina Department of Cultural Resources. Letter was sent on August 31, 1977, and discusses the approval to have Durward Center restore the Wurlitzer 125 band organ for the Pullen Park Carousel. Signed by Peter B. Sandbeck. There are several annotations made by Cy Farley, including "Finally!" written at the top, and "If you can make - it - call me Tues. A.M. --Thanks, Cy" written at the bottom, along with "Ann sending a copy to Royster."

Letter from Peter B. Sandbeck, Restoration Specialist at the North Carolina Department of Cultural Resources, to Mrs. William W. Farley on September 9, 1977. The letter discusses Cathy Leach's proposed paint removal experimental investigation for the Pullen Park Carousel, including suggestions for beginning the process and for record keeping. Annotation in the top margin includes a phone number, name, date, and time, written in black ink.

Letter to Dr. H.R. Chamblee, Jr. from Durward R. Center on September 14, 1977. Paper has a letterhead that reads: "Historical Instrument Restorations, 2100 St. Paul Street, Baltimore, Maryland 21218 (301)752-4771." The letter includes a price estimate and details/requirements for Mr. Center to restore the Wurlitzer Style 125 band organ for the Pullen Park Carousel. Signed by Mr. Center at the bottom. Written in the bottom left in blue ink is a cc'd list of three people, including Mrs. Cy Farley.

Copy of minutes from a November 17, 1977 summit meeting called by Mrs. William Farley to discuss the Pullen Park Carousel restoration. The minutes discuss Tom Layton and Tracy Cameron's restoration approaches and procedures. Other updates are listed in the minutes including financial status and various reports about things including doors for the carousel and the band organ. Two pages total, stapled in the top left corner.

Copy of a memo from Peter Sandbeck on November 18, 1977 regarding the Pullen Park Carousel meeting with Raleigh Parks Department. The memo includes an outline of three approaches for the restoration: the historically accurate approach, a compromise, and the creative approach. Written at the top in light blue ink is "just more jazz."

Resume for Thomas C. Layton, Manager, Art Services and Restoration, Cedar Point, Inc. The resume discusses his career as an artist, including his restoration work and carousel work. Resume is two pages total, stapled in the top left corner.
Black and white headshot photograph of Thomas C. Layton wearing a suit and tie. Printed on photo paper and three-hole punched on the left side.

Work proposal from the Overhead Door Company of Raleigh, NC to Joel Wittkamp regarding the doors for the carousel enclosure at Pullen Park. The proposal includes details about the doors, a price estimate of $16,830.00, and an approximation of 5-6 weeks for delivery and 2 weeks installation time. Dated to October 21, 1976.

Work proposal from Carolina Builders Corporation of Raleigh, NC to Dr. Wittkamp at N.C. State University for doors for the Pullen Park Carousel enclosure. Proposal includes details of the doors and a price estimate of $18,200.00. Dated to November 19, 1976.

Letter from Charles W. Springman to Rachael Smith Farley on September 29, 1977. The letter discusses the potential opportunities regarding the Merry-Go-Round film and details of the grant from the National Endowment for the Arts. Signed at the bottom by Charles W. Springman as "Charlie."

Copy of a letter from Tracey Cameron to Cy Farley from September 25, 1977. The letter expresses Cameron's interest in the carousel figures, but not the scenery panels, and includes a proposal for the process of restoring and repainting the figures. Cameron estimates that the restoration would take less than one year and would cost $400 per figure as a base price. Cameron also states her preference to work in Hartford, Connecticut. The final page is signed by Cameron. Three pages total, stapled in the top left corner. The back of the third page has some notes written in blue ink.

Copy of a statement for carousel organ restoration that provides a brief history of automatic musical instruments from the early 19th century through the Great Depression in the 1930s. The statement describes some of the work that Mr. Durwood (Durward) Center is doing to restore the band organ for the Pullen Park Carousel. Two pages total, stapled in the top left corner.

Address label that reads: 
"Please forward all correspondence to my home address: 
Thomas C. Layton
918 W. Monroe Street 
Sandusky, Ohio 44870
Ph. 1 (410) 625 7271"

Copy of the National Register of Historic Places Inventory - Nomination Form for the Pullen Park Carousel. Includes a description of the carousel and each animal figure. "Tom Layton" is written at the top of the first page in red ink. Eleven pages total, stapled in the top left corner.
Business card for the Overhead Door Company of Raleigh, Inc. P.O. Box 27404 Raleigh, N.C. 27611. Tim Harward, Phone: 876-0637

Overhead Door Corporation catalog for metal rolling doors, grilles, and shutters. The front cover has a collage of nine images. The back cover advertises their warranty and a few other products with accompanying pictures. Written in pink ink on the front is "Rolling Steel Service Doors page 5 & 6, Door size will be 12' x 12'."

Copy of an application: Request for Historic Preservation Grant-In-Aid from the N.C. Department of Cultural Resources Division of Archives and History. Applicant is Mrs. James B. Turner, Jr., President of The Raleigh Fine Arts Society, Inc., for the Pullen Park Dentzel Carousel.

File folder that holds papers PPC2024.002.054-PPC2024.002.065. Writing in blue ink on the folder includes "$600.00," the label "[illegible] for overhead doors," and "40 Building." Printed on the inside of the folder is "Oxford Stock No. 752 1/3, Made in U.S.A."

Resume of works and experience for Ruby Newman of San Francisco, California. Includes work experience and education from 1968-1978. Work experience includes painting and restoration of the Golden Gate Park Carousel. Two pages total, stapled in the top left corner.

Copy of a letter from Larry E. Tise, State Historic Preservation Officer, to Mr. Frank Evans, Director of Parks and Recreation Department of the City of Raleigh, and Mrs. Rachael S. Farley, Chairman of Carousel Restoration for the Raleigh Fine Arts Society. The letter notifies them of the grant-in-aid awarded to them for $5,000, as well as administrative deadlines related to the grant. More details of the grant fund requirements are also outlined. Signed by Larry E. Tise and dated to March 10, 1978. Two pages total, stapled in the top left corner.

Copy of a letter from Janet K. Seapker, Grants-in-Aid Administrator for the NC Department of Cultural Resources, to Mr. Frank Evans, Director of Parks and Recreation Department for the City of Raleigh, dated to April 18, 1978. The letter discusses deadlines and arrangements for a grant for the Pullen Park Carousel. Signed by Janet K. Seapker. Mrs. Rachael S. Farley is cc'd. Portions of the letter have been bracketed and underlined in blue ink with a note in the margin that reads: "this was the usual."

Copy of notes from Colonel Ed Gilbert, Greenfield Village, Henry Ford Museum Conservation Center, regarding the restoration of the carousel from 1978. Notes include materials and certain processes used, as well as contact information for Dr. Robert L. Fellow, an expert on resins. Notes in purple ink are written in the top margin: "Ann Walker visit to Greenfield, Summer 1978."

Copy of two pages of minutes from the meeting at Department of Archives and History with Peter Sandbeck, Cy Farley, Ann Turner, and Ann Walker. The meeting took place on Monday, August 21, 1978. The meeting discussed grants received, as well as Rosa Regan's (Ragan) progress on stripping paint on the Pullen Park Carousel animals so far, and how to proceed from then on. Ann V. Walker, Secretary was the notetaker. The copy of the minutes is annotated with blue ink, including brackets and underlining on the first page, and a note on the second page that reads: "of course this never happened, don't ask us why!" pointing to an underlined section of text.

September 1978 edition of "Spotlight," a newsletter sponsored by CP&L, Carolina Power and Light Company, Raleigh, North Carolina. The cover shows Rosa Ragan working on one of the Pullen Park Carousel animals. Pages 4-5 include a short article about the carousel restoration titled, "Hurdy-Gurdy Time." The article talks about the history of the carousel, the work being done by Ragan, and includes a testimony about the carousel by J.W.P. Hodges. Pages 4-5 also showcase images of the carousel animals, as well as Rosa Ragan working on an animal, and J.W.P. Hodges riding the carousel with his grandson.

a) newsletter
b) note that was paperclipped to newsletter

Handwritten note that was paperclipped to the September 1978 Spotlight newsletter. The note is written in blue ink and reads: "Cy, thought you might be interested in one of our non-political brochures! Helen H. Cover + p. 4-5." Note was written on folded paper, but the inside and back are blank.

a) newsletter
b) note

Copy of a letter to Mrs. Cy Farley from Patsy Rogers, Coordinator, Titles II & VI for the City of Raleigh CETA Program on September 15, 1978. The letter contains details of the Fine Arts project including funding timeline limitations, as well as steps to activate the Fine Arts Project which was approved by the Raleigh Consortium Advisory Council. Two pages total, stapled in top left corner. "Page 2'" was stapled as the first page. The second page has a note in light blue ink that reads: "CETA grant was to us. Frank has trouble even realizing this." A section of the text is also marked.
